newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government wins transport confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy government wins transport confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won a vote of confidence in the upper house of parliament (Senate) on Wednesday on a bill covering the reorganisation of the transport sector, a parliamentary official said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government won a similar do-or-die vote on the same bill in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) last week as it bids to meet tight new deadlines for the ratification of cabinet decree laws.

Wednesday's vote was won by 155 to 84, meaning that the transport decree, which will reform the fiscal system for the sector and cut the number of motorway tariffs for haulage companies, has become law.
The government relies on support from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for its majority in the lower house but controls the Senate without outside backing.

The government has resorted to numerous confidence votes in recent months after a Constitutional court decision which banned the cabinet from the traditional practice of re-issuing old decrees, giving it just 60 days to push the bills into law.

The court ruling posed a legislative nightmare, making it virtually impossible for the government to push decrees onto the statute books without recourse to a confidence vote, unless it gets the go-ahead from the opposition. If expiring decrees are not turned into law in time they must be discarded.

The centre-right opposition had proposed numerous changes to the transport decree but the government said that the court ruling meant it did not have time to discuss the amendments and instead had to sweep them away with the confidence motions.
The government last week also comfortably won a vote of confidence in the chamber to brush aside hundreds of opposition amendments to the final part of the 1997 austerity budget.
